title: Supreme Court: A High Court that refuses anticipatory bail cannot also direct how regular bail is to be handled
case_name: Jagannath Mandangi v. State of Odisha
citation: Order dated 26 October 2026 in SLP (Crl.) Nos. 6555-6559 of 2026 (reported as 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1114); neutral citation not confirmed
card_summary: The Supreme Court partly set aside an Orissa High Court order that refused anticipatory bail but also told the accused to surrender and apply for regular bail within two weeks. The refusal stood. The directions on regular bail were removed, since the trial court decides that on the material before it, at the time of the application.
card_tip: An order refusing anticipatory bail should be read for any extra directions; those can be challenged separately.
verification_notes: Topic chosen: criminal bail items dominated LiveLaw daily round-ups and Delhi HC pronouncement lists seen on 9 Nov 2026 (Criminal Law is the heaviest category in the headlines seen); no search-volume figures were seen or are claimed.
